---
title: "17 · Metapaths and the 15-minute city"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

A metapath is a semantic relation between two nodes established through a
sequence of intermediate steps: instead of "restaurant A touches segment 7,
which touches segment 8, which touches bar B" you get a direct
**restaurant A → bar B** edge labeled with what it cost to get there. The
clustering workflow of notebook 18 rests on it.

The street network is built as a graph of connectors weighted by walking time,
then both implementations are applied: `add_metapaths()`, controlled by hop
count over a given sequence of relations, and `add_metapaths_by_weight()`, which
projects by **accumulated cost**, connecting two nodes when a path exists whose
total weight stays under a threshold. With the weight set to travel time and the
threshold at 900 s, that projection *is* the 15-minute city.

Two operator divergences show up here: `create_street_dual_graph` drops the
`key` level of the OSMnx index and collapses parallel segments, and
`c2g_graph_tool_apply` with `ISOCHRONE` works on local Blender coordinates with
no cost attribute, so its threshold counts hops rather than time. Because
15-minute accessibility over a neighborhood is very nearly a complete graph,
the renders use the edge backbone materialized in the data
(`SciGraphs.api.thin`), so every renderer sees the same sparsification.
